claim: Substance use, including cigarettes and cannabis, is associated with poorer sustained attention in late adolescence and early adulthood.
source: Substance use, including cigarettes and cannabis, is associated with poorer sustained attention in late adolescence and early adulthood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known association, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Behaviors and brain connectivity associated with diminished sustained attention at age 14 predicted subsequent increases in cannabis and cigarette smoking.
source: Behaviors and brain connectivity associated with diminished sustained attention at age 14 predicted subsequent increases in cannabis and cigarette smoking, establishing sustained attention as a robust biomarker for vulnerability to substance use.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the latent change score model analysis presented in the results section.

claim: Individual differences in network strength relevant to sustained attention were preserved across developmental stages.
source: Individual differences in network strength relevant to sustained attention were preserved across developmental stages and sustained attention networks generalized to participants in an external dataset.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analyses showing significant correlations of network strength between timepoints.

claim: Sustained attention networks generalized to participants in an external dataset.
source: Individual differences in network strength relevant to sustained attention were preserved across developmental stages and sustained attention networks generalized to participants in an external dataset.
evidence: This is demonstrated by applying models to the STRATIFY dataset with significant predictive performance.

claim: Brain networks of sustained attention are robust, consistent, and able to predict aspects of later substance use.
source: In summary, brain networks of sustained attention are robust, consistent, and able to predict aspects of later substance use.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Sustained attention is a critical cognitive process in daily life, playing a significant role in academic achievement, social communication, and mental health.
source: Sustained attention is a critical cognitive process in daily life, playing a significant role in academic achievement, social communication, and mental health (Esterman and Rothlein, 2019)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Esterman and Rothlein, 2019.

claim: Sustained attention can be defined as the focus on performance on a single task over time, with the goal of explaining both the fluctuations within an individual as well as the individual differences in overall ability to maintain stable task performance.
source: can be defined as "the focus on performance on a single task over time, with the goal of explaining both the fluctuations within an individual as well as the individual differences in overall ability to maintain stable task performance" (p. 174) (Esterman and Rothlein, 2019).
evidence: This is a direct definition cited from Esterman and Rothlein, 2019.

claim: Sustained attention notably improves between the ages of 9 and 16.
source: Sustained attention notably improves between the ages of 9 and 16 (Thomson et al., 2022)
evidence: This developmental pattern is supported by citation to Thomson et al., 2022.

claim: The functional neuroanatomy of sustained attention involves cingulate, prefrontal, and parietal cortices; supplementary motor area; frontal eye field; and cerebellum.
source: The functional neuroanatomy of sustained attention involves cingulate, prefrontal, and parietal cortices; supplementary motor area; frontal eye field; and cerebellum (Bauer et al., 2020; Pinar et al., 2018).
evidence: This neuroanatomical description is supported by citations to Bauer et al., 2020 and Pinar et al., 2018.

claim: Adolescents (14–17 years of age) using cannabis a minimum of 4 days per week for at least the last 6 months showed impaired sustained attention in the rapid visual information processing (RVP) task.
source: For instance, adolescents (14–17 years of age) using cannabis a minimum of 4 days per week for at least the last 6 months showed impaired sustained attention in the rapid visual information processing (RVP) task, and in the immediate memory task versus non-users (Dougherty et al., 2013).
evidence: This finding is cited from Dougherty et al., 2013.

claim: Adolescents (12–17 years of age) in a high tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) group exhibited lower accuracy on the RVP task than a low THC group.
source: Adolescents (12–17 years of age) in a high tetrahydrocannabinol (THC, the primary psychoactive component in cannabis) group exhibited lower accuracy on the RVP task than a low THC group (Shannon et al., 2010).
evidence: This finding is cited from Shannon et al., 2010.

claim: Cigarette users aged 18–29 showed significant cognitive impairments in sustained attention than non-smokers in the RVP task.
source: Cigarette users aged 18–29 showed significant cognitive impairments in sustained attention than non-smokers in the RVP task (Chamberlain et al., 2012).
evidence: This finding is cited from Chamberlain et al., 2012.

claim: A systematic review of the next-day cognitive effects of heavy alcohol consumption demonstrated impairments in sustained attention during alcohol hangovers using meta-analysis.
source: A systematic review of the next-day cognitive effects of heavy alcohol consumption demonstrated impairments in sustained attention during alcohol hangovers using meta-analysis (Yakir et al., 2007).
evidence: This finding is cited from Yakir et al., 2007.

claim: Poor sustained attention was associated with the increased probability of adolescents subsequently initiating cigarette smoking between ages 11 and 13.
source: Poor sustained attention, unlike other neurocognitive functions such as working memory, attention flexibility, or perceptual sensitivity, was associated with the increased probability of adolescents subsequently initiating cigarette smoking between ages 11 and 13 and with a higher chance of being a daily smoker by age 16.
evidence: This finding is from Harakeh et al., 2012, as cited in the text.

claim: Poor sustained attention was associated with a higher chance of being a daily smoker by age 16.
source: Poor sustained attention, unlike other neurocognitive functions such as working memory, attention flexibility, or perceptual sensitivity, was associated with the increased probability of adolescents subsequently initiating cigarette smoking between ages 11 and 13 and with a higher chance of being a daily smoker by age 16.
evidence: This finding is from Harakeh et al., 2012, as cited in the text.

claim: A meta-analysis identified common neural alterations in primary dorsal striatal, and frontal circuits, engaged in reward/salience processing, habit formation, and executive control across various substances (nicotine, cannabis, alcohol, and cocaine).
source: A meta-analysis identified common neural alterations in primary dorsal striatal, and frontal circuits, engaged in reward/salience processing, habit formation, and executive control across various substances (nicotine, cannabis, alcohol, and cocaine) (Thiele and Bellgrove, 2018).
evidence: This finding is cited from Thiele and Bellgrove, 2018.

claim: 90% of cannabis users smoke cigarettes during their lifetime.
source: Agrawal et al., 2012, reported that 90% of cannabis users smoke cigarettes during their lifetime
evidence: This statistic is cited from Agrawal et al., 2012.

claim: The widespread co-use of cannabis and cigarettes may be attributed to genetic sharing and similar neural mechanisms.
source: and the widespread co-use of the two may be attributed to genetic sharing (Agrawal et al., 2010; Yadav et al., 2016) and similar neural mechanisms (Klugah-Brown et al., 2020).
evidence: This explanation is supported by citations to Agrawal et al., 2010; Yadav et al., 2016; and Klugah-Brown et al., 2020.

claim: Functional brain networks can predict various behavioral traits, such as substance use and sustained attention.
source: Functional brain networks can predict various behavioral traits, such as substance use (Yip et al., 2019) and sustained attention (Rosenberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This capability is supported by citations to Yip et al., 2019 and Rosenberg et al., 2016.

claim: Lower sustained attention has been accompanied by both stronger reductions in neural activity in the visual cortex and stronger recruitment of the right supramarginal gyrus with increasing time on a sustained attention task with central cues in cigarette smokers as opposed to non-smokers.
source: Lower sustained attention has been accompanied by both stronger reductions in neural activity in the visual cortex and stronger recruitment of the right supramarginal gyrus with increasing time on a sustained attention task with central cues in cigarette smokers as opposed to non-smokers (Vossel et al., 2011).
evidence: This finding is cited from Vossel et al., 2011.

claim: Cannabis users aged 16–26 had stronger connectivity between the left posterior cingulate cortex and the cerebellum, correlated with poorer performance on sustained attention/working memory and verbal learning measures.
source: In a resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) paradigm, cannabis users aged 16–26 had stronger connectivity between the left posterior cingulate cortex and the cerebellum, correlated with poorer performance on sustained attention/working memory and verbal learning measures (Ritchay et al., 2021).
evidence: This finding is cited from Ritchay et al., 2021.

claim: Functional connectivity during task performance has demonstrated superiority in predicting individual behaviors and traits compared to resting-state fMRI.
source: Although most brain connectomic research has utilized resting-state fMRI data, functional connectivity (FC) during task performance has demonstrated superiority in predicting individual behaviors and traits, due to its potential to capture more behaviorally relevant information (Dhamala et al., 2023; Greene et al., 2018; Yoo et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dhamala et al., 2023; Greene et al., 2018; and Yoo et al., 2018.

claim: Task-related FC outperforms both typical task-based and resting-state FC in predicting individual differences.
source: Specifically, Zhao et al., 2023, suggested that task-related FC outperforms both typical task-based and resting-state FC in predicting individual differences.
evidence: This claim is cited from Zhao et al., 2023.

claim: ICV at age 14 was significantly higher than ICV at ages 19 and 23.
source: Post hoc analysis showed that ICV decreased with age: ICV at age 14 was significantly higher than ICV at ages 19 (t=6.535, p<0.001) and 23 (t=10.109, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the linear mixed model analysis.

claim: ICV at age 19 was significantly higher than that at age 23.
source: ICV at age 19 was also significantly higher than that at age 23 (t=4.768, p<0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the linear mixed model analysis.

claim: Elevated dopamine and noradrenaline levels in the prefrontal cortex lead to improved sustained attention in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Elevated dopamine and noradrenaline levels in the prefrontal cortex lead to improved sustained attention in a dose-dependent manner (Marshall et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from Marshall et al., 2019.

claim: Methylphenidate increases both noradrenaline and dopamine signaling and improves sustained attention.
source: In humans, methylphenidate, a psychostimulant commonly used to treat ADHD, increases both noradrenaline and dopamine signaling and improves sustained attention (Dockree et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from Dockree et al., 2017.

claim: Low basal dopamine levels are markers of vulnerability for increased drug administration.
source: More importantly, studies in primates (Morgan et al., 2002; Nader et al., 2006), rodents (Dalley et al., 2007; Trifilieff et al., 2017), and humans (Casey et al., 2014; Trifilieff and Martinez, 2014; Volkow et al., 2006) have indicated that low basal dopamine levels are markers of vulnerability for increased drug administration.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations across species.

claim: Blunted dopamine release may precede the development of addiction in humans.
source: For example, Casey et al., 2014, demonstrated that blunted dopamine release may precede the development of addiction in humans.
evidence: This is cited from Casey et al., 2014.

claim: There is a negative correlation between baseline D2 receptor availability and rates of cocaine self-administration in monkeys.
source: Nader et al., 2006, found a negative correlation between baseline D2 receptor availability and rates of cocaine self-administration in monkeys.
evidence: This is cited from Nader et al., 2006.

claim: 18–23% of cigarette smokers aged 12–17 met the criteria for cannabis use disorder, in contrast to only 2% of non-smoking youth.
source: A national survey in America indicated that 18–23% of cigarette smokers aged 12–17 met the criteria for cannabis use disorder, in contrast to only 2% of non-smoking youth (Weinberger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from Weinberger et al., 2018.

claim: 80.8% of cigarette smokers engage in cannabis consumption.
source: Another national online survey in the UK reported that 80.8% of cigarette smokers engage in cannabis consumption, indicating a prevalent practice of co-administering cannabis and tobacco through smoking (Hindocha et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from Hindocha et al., 2021.

claim: There is a strong and significant genetic correlation between lifetime cannabis use and lifetime cigarette smoking.
source: Yadav et al., 2016, demonstrated a strong and significant genetic correlation between lifetime cannabis use and lifetime cigarette smoking within a large cohort of 32,330 participants, suggesting a high degree of genetic sharing between the two.
evidence: This is cited from Yadav et al., 2016.

claim: Individuals who used cannabis, smoked tobacco, or engaged in co-use exhibited larger gray matter volumes in the left putamen compared to healthy controls.
source: Using neuroimaging techniques, Wetherill et al., 2015, indicated that individuals who used cannabis, smoked tobacco, or engaged in co-use exhibited larger gray matter volumes in the left putamen compared to healthy controls.
evidence: This is cited from Wetherill et al., 2015.

claim: Both nicotine and cannabis have similar effects on mesolimbic dopaminergic pathways, modulating dopamine release in the striatum.
source: Both nicotine and cannabis have similar effects on mesolimbic dopaminergic pathways engaged, modulating dopamine release in the striatum (Bossong et al., 2009; Dongelmans et al., 2021).
evidence: This is cited from Bossong et al., 2009 and Dongelmans et al., 2021.

claim: The strength of the sustained attention brain network was robustly correlated with RVP task performance rather than other cognitive measures.
source: The strength of the sustained attention brain network was robustly correlated with RVP task performance, a typical sustained attention task, rather than other cognitive measures (Supplementary file 1l).
evidence: This demonstrates the specificity of the sustained attention networks.

claim: A notable enhancement in sustained attention (i.e. decreased ICV) was observed from ages 14 to 23.
source: A notable enhancement in sustained attention (i.e. decreased ICV) was observed from ages 14 to 23, as expected (Fortenbaugh et al., 2015; Williams et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a finding from the study consistent with prior literature.

claim: Sustained attention networks derived from Go and Successful stop trials predicted behavior at different timepoints, implying that individual differences in sustained attention and associated networks were preserved throughout development.
source: Sustained attention networks derived from Go and Successful stop trials predicted behavior at different timepoints, implying that individual differences in sustained attention and associated networks were preserved throughout development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cross-timepoint prediction results.

claim: In neurodiverse youth, attention networks in individuals remained stable across months to years.
source: Previously, in neurodiverse youth, attention networks in individuals remained stable across months to years (Sisk et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from Sisk et al., 2022.

claim: The same functional connections predicting overall sustained attention ability also forecasted attentional changes observed over minutes, days, weeks, and months.
source: Rosenberg et al., 2020, also illustrated that the same functional connections predicting overall sustained attention ability also forecasted attentional changes observed over minutes, days, weeks, and months.

claim: Poorer sustained attention and strength of the associated brain networks at age 14 predicted greater increases in cannabis and cigarette smoking from ages 14 to 23.
source: Poorer sustained attention and strength of the associated brain networks at age 14 predicted greater increases in cannabis and cigarette smoking from ages 14 to 23.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on the latent change score model results.

claim: RT variability is a straightforward measure of sustained attention, with increasing variability thought to reflect poor sustained attention.
source: Reaction time (RT) variability is a straightforward measure of sustained attention, with increasing variability thought to reflect poor sustained attention.
evidence: This is a definition based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: RT variability can be defined as the intra-individual coefficient of variation (ICV), calculated as the standard deviation of Go RT divided by the mean Go RT from Go trials in the stop signal task.
source: RT variability can be defined as the intra-individual coefficient of variation (ICV), calculated as the standard deviation of Go RT divided by the mean Go RT from Go trials in the stop signal task.
evidence: This is the operational definition used in the study.

claim: Lower ICV indicates better sustained attention.
source: Lower ICV indicates better sustained attention.
evidence: This is the interpretation of the ICV measure used in the study.

claim: IMAGEN is a large longitudinal study that recruited over 2000 participants aged 14–23 in Europe.
source: All neuroimaging data and behavioral data were obtained from the IMAGEN study. IMAGEN is a large longitudinal study that recruited over 2000 participants aged 14–23 in Europe (Kaiser et al., 2022).
evidence: This describes the dataset used in the study.

claim: STRATIFY is a sub-dataset within IMAGEN that recruits fMRI data from patients aged 23.
source: In addition, we used an independent dataset STRATIFY as external validation for age 23. STRATIFY (N = ~300) is a sub-dataset within IMAGEN that recruits fMRI data from patients aged 23.
evidence: This describes the external validation dataset.

claim: The stop signal task required participants to respond to a Go signal (arrows pointing left/right) by pressing the left/right button while withholding their response if the Go signal was unpredictably followed by a Stop signal (arrows pointing upward).
source: The stop signal task required participants to respond to a Go signal (arrows pointing left/right) by pressing the left/right button while withholding their response if the Go signal was unpredictably followed by a Stop signal (arrows pointing upward).

claim: CPM is a data-driven method that can examine individual differences in brain connectivity.
source: CPM is a data-driven method that can examine individual differences in brain connectivity (Shen et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, cited from Shen et al., 2017.

claim: Task-related FC outperforms resting-state FC in predicting individual behaviors and traits due to its potential to capture more behaviorally relevant information.
source: Although most brain connectomic research has utilized resting-state fMRI data, functional connectivity (FC) during task performance has demonstrated superiority in predicting individual behaviors and traits, due to its potential to capture more behaviorally relevant information (Dhamala et al., 2023; Greene et al., 2018; Yoo et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a rationale for the methodological choice, supported by citations.

claim: The bivariate latent change score model allows quantification of bidirectional longitudinal relations between substance use and both behaviors and brain activity associated with sustained attention.
source: A latent change score model can quantify bidirectional longitudinal relations between substance use and both behaviors and brain activity associated with sustained attention, shedding light on how substance use impacts sustained attention and its associated brain activity, and vice versa.
evidence: This describes the analytical approach used to test directionality.

claim: There are linear relationships between substance use and sustained attention over time.
source: Additionally, previous cross-sectional and longitudinal studies (Broyd et al., 2016; Harakeh et al., 2012; Lisdahl and Price, 2012) have shown that there are linear relationships between substance use and sustained attention over time.
evidence: This is based on prior literature cited in the text.

claim: No significant differences in cigarette and cannabis use were observed between individuals with lower and higher working memory at baseline during the strategy working memory (SWM) task.
source: Unlike sustained attention, no significant differences in cigarette and cannabis use were observed between individuals with lower and higher working memory at baseline during the strategy working memory (SWM) task (Supplementary file 1w and Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This demonstrates the specificity of sustained attention in predicting substance use.

claim: Sustained attention notably improves concomitant with cognitive maturation and brain development during adolescence.
source: Sustained attention notably improves between the ages of 9 and 16 (Thomson et al., 2022), concomitant with cognitive maturation and brain development during adolescence (Paus, 2005).
evidence: This links developmental changes in sustained attention to broader neurodevelopmental processes.
